1.name: Druidic
1.notes:
You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids. While learning this ancient tongue, you also unlocked the magic of communicating with animals; you always have the Speak with Animals spell prepared.

You can use Druidic to leave hidden messages. You and others who know Druidic automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check but can't decipher it without magic.

1.name: Primal Order
1.notes:
You dedicate yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.

Magician. You know one extra cantrip from the Druid spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to nature gives you a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Nature) checks. The bonus equals your Wisdom modifier (minimum +1).

Warden. Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and Medium armor.

1.name: Spellcasting
1.notes:
You have learned to cast spells through studying the mystical forces of nature.

Cantrips. You know two cantrips of your choice from the Druid spell list. Druidcraft and Produce Flame are recommended. Whenever you gain a Druid level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another Druid cantrip of your choice. At levels 4 and 10, you learn an additional cantrip, as shown in the class table.

Spell Slots. The Druid Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Druid spells of level 1+ that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 Druid spells. Animal Friendship, Cure Wounds, Faerie Fire, and Thunderwave are recommended. The number of prepared spells increases as you gain Druid levels, as shown in the class table. The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
If another Druid feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare, but they otherwise count as Druid spells for you.

Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of them with other Druid spells for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Druid spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Druid spells.

2.name: Wild Companion
2.notes:
You can summon a nature spirit that assumes an animal form to aid you. As a Magic action, you can expend a spell slot or a use of Wild Shape to cast the Find Familiar spell without Material components.

When you cast the spell in this way, the familiar is Fey and disappears when you finish a Long Rest.

2.name: Wild Shape
2.notes:
The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a Bonus Action, you transform into a Beast form that you have learned for this feature (see Known Forms below). You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level or until you use Wild Shape again, become Incapacitated, or die. You can also end the form early as a Bonus Action.

Number of Uses. You can use Wild Shape twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest and all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You gain additional uses at higher levels, as shown in the class table.

Known Forms. You know four Beast forms, chosen from Beast stat blocks with a maximum Challenge Rating of 1/4 and without a Fly Speed. Rat, Riding Horse, Spider, and Wolf are recommended. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your known forms with another eligible form.
As you gain levels, your number of known forms and the maximum CR of those forms increase, as shown in the Beast Shapes table (see beast_shapes_table). Starting at level 8, you can adopt a form that has a Fly Speed.
When choosing known forms, you may look in the Monster Manual or elsewhere for eligible Beasts if your DM allows it.

Rules While Transformed. While in a Beast form, you retain your personality, memories, and ability to speak, and the following rules apply:

• Temporary Hit Points. When you assume a Wild Shape form, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Druid level.

• Game Statistics. Your game statistics are replaced by the Beast’s stat block, but you retain your creature type; Hit Points; Hit Point Dice; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. You also retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies and use your Proficiency Bonus for them, in addition to gaining the proficiencies of the creature. If a skill or saving throw modifier in the Beast’s stat block is higher than yours, use the higher value.

• No Spellcasting. You can’t cast spells, but shape-shifting doesn’t break your Concentration or otherwise interfere with a spell you’ve already cast.

• Objects and Equipment. Your ability to handle objects is determined by the form’s limbs. You choose whether your equipment falls in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the DM decides whether it is practical for the form to wear specific items. Your equipment does not change size or shape to match the form, and any equipment the form cannot wear must either fall to the ground or merge with the form. Equipment that merges has no effect while you are in that form.

3.name: Subclass Feature
3.notes: You gain a Druid subclass of your choice and its level 3 feature. You gain additional subclass features at higher Druid levels.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Druid levels 8, 12, and 16.

5.name: Wild Resurgence
5.notes:
Once on each of your turns, if you have no uses of Wild Shape left, you can give yourself one use by expending a spell slot (no action required).

In addition, you can expend one use of Wild Shape (no action required) to give yourself a level 1 spell slot. You can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

6.name: Subclass Feature
6.notes: You gain a level 6 feature from your Druid subclass.

7.name: Elemental Fury
7.notes:
The might of the elements flows through you. Choose one of the following options:

• Potent Spellcasting. Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Druid cantrip.

• Primal Strike. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon or a Beast form’s attack while in Wild Shape, you can cause the target to take an extra 1d8 Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage (you choose the damage type when you hit).

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
8.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

10.name: Subclass Feature
10.notes: You gain a level 10 feature from your Druid subclass.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
12.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

14.name: Subclass Feature
14.notes: You gain a level 14 feature from your Druid subclass.

15.name: Improved Elemental Fury
15.notes:
The option you chose for Elemental Fury grows more powerful:

• Potent Spellcasting. When you cast a Druid cantrip with a range of 10 feet or greater, its range increases by 300 feet.

• Primal Strike. The extra damage of your Primal Strike increases to 2d8.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
16.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

18.name: Beast Spells
18.notes: While using Wild Shape, you can cast spells in Beast form, except for any spell that has a Material component with a specified cost or that consumes its Material component.

19.name: Epic Boon
19.notes: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Dimensional Travel is recommended.

20.name: Archdruid
20.notes:
The vitality of nature constantly blooms within you, granting the following benefits:

• Evergreen Wild Shape. Whenever you roll Initiative and have no uses of Wild Shape left, you regain one expended use.

• Nature Magician. You can convert uses of Wild Shape into a spell slot (no action required). Choose a number of your unexpended uses of Wild Shape and convert them into a single spell slot, with each use contributing 2 spell levels (for example, two uses become a level 4 slot). Once you use this benefit, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

• Longevity. The primal magic you wield slows your aging. For every ten years that pass, your body ages only one year.
